gear.h2: Every amp, cab and pedal ships with the app, with no packs to buy.
gear.lede: Built-in models, NAM captures of real amps and pedals, cab IRs and LV2 and VST3 plugins all load into the same chain.
captures.h2: A NAM capture pack becomes one amp with a Gain knob.
captures.lede: Packs ship one .nam file per gain setting, and OpenRig loads the right one as you turn the knob, so you never scroll a file list mid-song.
captures.c1.h3: NAM A1 and A2 at full size
captures.c1.p: A2 captures run as they were trained; the model is never shrunk to save CPU.
captures.c2.p: Point a block at a .nam or a cab IR on your disk and it plays like any amp in the catalog.
captures.c3.p: A NAM amp, a built-in drive and a VST3 reverb sit in the same chain, in any order.
captures.shotCap: The Marshall 1959 SLP plugin: the CAPTURE tab picks the .nam, the AMP tab shapes it.
rig.h2: Split the signal into a Marshall and an AC30, then blend them back into one.
rig.lede: Each path gets its own amp and cab, and the mix block sets how much of A and B you hear before the delay and reverb.
rig.h3: The compact view puts every knob of the chain on one screen, in signal order.
rig.lede2: Tweak the drive, the split and the amp side by side without opening a single window.
rig.n1.p: Move a pedal before or after the amp and hear the difference right away.
rig.n2.p: Save the whole chain as a preset and switch between verse, chorus and solo scenes with one tap.
rig.n3.p: MIDI Learn assigns any knob or switch to your controller, and an M-Vave Chocolate comes mapped.
band.h2: Guitar, acoustic and vocals play at the same time, each through its own chain.
band.lede: Every instrument gets its own inputs, gear and outputs, so a change on the vocal mic never touches the guitar.
inst.i1.p: Amps, cabs and the whole pedalboard.
inst.i2.p: Body models, mic chain and room.
inst.i4.p: A generic chain for whatever you plug in.
inst.note: Bass and keys rigs are next.
band.shotCap: One tuner per active input: the lead and rhythm guitars at A, the acoustic waiting for a note.
